status_meaning.confirmed: held in every project where it could apply
status_meaning.provisional: held wherever seen, but too few cases to trust
status_meaning.contested: projects disagree — designer discretion, or a rule we cannot see yet
status_meaning.stated: told to us by the design team — not deduced from drawings, and outranks anything inferred

zones.note: Designers use different words for the same zone across projects. Canonicalise on import.

rules.statement: At each kitchen corner, the base blind cabinet (including LeMans) and its wall blind cabinet must be on the same wall. If the base blind cabinet is on wall A, the wall blind cabinet must also be on wall A, never on adjacent wall B. A base blind corner requires its matching wall blind cabinet only where its own wall has a wall cabinet zone running into that corner; if that wall has no upper zone there, the base blind stands alone and nothing is reported. Where the upper zone exists and the wall blind cannot fit, report a problem instead of moving it to the adjacent wall.
rules.note: Match each physical corner separately. Base and wall cabinets retain their own catalogue widths and depths. Relaxed by the designer 2026-10-13: a missing upper zone on the blind's wall no longer blocks the corner.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs blindCornerProblems() checks only base blinds whose wall has a wall zone reaching the corner; corners() places the wall blind on the owner wall when that zone exists. Test: test/blind-corners/blind-corners.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Within each drawn cabinet zone, cabinets, fixed panels, legal fillers and explicitly reserved or concealed spaces cover the usable run exactly. Openings and shared corner footprints remain clear; no physical space is filled twice.

Base and wall cabinets may share the same wall span because they occupy different heights. A tall cabinet owns its entire physical footprint from floor to top: no separate base, wall or tall cabinet may occupy that space, on the same wall or around an adjacent corner. Reserved footprint markers are not cabinets. Resolve corner ownership before packing; if no legal arrangement exists, report the conflict by name.
evidence: 88 of 88 swept rooms had a blind corner placed under the fridge tower because corners were resolved before the tall band was projected down — the layout was reported REJECTED and still drawn.
rules.note: Reserve tall footprints before base and wall corners and before packing each neighbouring tall run. Every insertion checks same-wall occupancy and final physical volume validation checks all walls.

rules.statement: Historical evidence showed several service items retained from drawings. The engine requires main sink, hob and refrigerator anchors and supports an optional independently placed veggie sink.
evidence: P1: architect's hob, fridge and dw positions all retained
P3: architect's hob (bottom), sink (right wall) and fridge (top right) all retained
P4: architect's refrigerator (top left), hob+OTG (top), sink bowl and dishwasher (bottom left) all retained
rules.note: Superseded by anchors-are-designer-input. Dishwasher is solver-placed and optional. Kept only as historical evidence.

rules.statement: Items with no service constraint — tall units, storage — are placed by the designer and may be moved off the architect's suggestion.
evidence: P2: architect labelled TALL UNITS on the bottom wall; designer put the tall run on the left and gave the bottom wall to the wet zone

rules.statement: Do not convert the architect's stated size. Finished dimensions come from site measurement and are always smaller, by an amount that is not derivable.
rules.note: Deduction ranges -16 to -68 across four projects. Not a constant, not derivable.

rules.statement: Provide a usable corner cabinet. Up to 100mm of concealed space behind a blind corner cabinet is allowed when it improves shutter alignment or cabinet fit; this space stays empty and needs no filler. A BASE corner takes a blind unit — BB-SH 1150, or BB-AC-LMC LeMans 1050. A TALL corner takes a tall blind (TB 1150) and never a LeMans. Wall and loft blind are 900; full-depth loft blind (LBF) is 1050.
evidence: P1 base blind corner
P2 base blind cabinet
P3 two base blind cabinets
P4 base blind cabinet + wall blind shutter
rules.note: LeMans is a base-only fitting. Widths confirmed: LeMans 1050, blind 1150 — choosing between them shifts the run by 100mm, so the corner choice feeds back into the packing constraint.
rules.deferred: L-corner units (BLC / WLC / TLC) are a planned third strategy, not in scope yet. Their codes are 10 fields (no P3); the catalogue parses them but layout never places them yet.

rules.statement: A base corner uses the LeMans unit BB-AC-...-LMC-... at 1050 wide. It is a distinct catalogue product, not a fitting added to the 1150 blind unit.
rules.open_question: Width is settled at 1050. What is not settled is WHEN LeMans is used instead of the 1150 blind — 3 of 4 projects used it, P2 did not.
rules.note: Now 3 of 4 projects. P2 remains the only corner without it — and since LeMans is 1050 and plain blind is 1150, P2's corner should be checkable against its own run arithmetic.

rules.statement: At least one bottle pullout is required. It may sit immediately beside the hob or immediately beyond either cabinet flanking the hob. Use a catalogue width of 150 or 300 according to the available space.
evidence: P3: 600 | 150 BPO | 900 hob | 150 BPO | 600  (both sides)
P4: 600 | 600 hob | 300 BPO                  (right side only)
rules.note: Do not force the bottle pullout between the hob and a designer-selected flanking cabinet. At least one must occupy an allowed position.

rules.statement: Bottle pullouts by kitchen size, measured as the total length of the drawn base zones: under 3000mm exactly one; 3000-5000mm at most two; over 5000mm at most three. An extra one becomes a plain cabinet of its width, or merges with the plain cabinet beside it when the two make exactly one plain width. It never leaves a filler behind (no-filler-between-cabinets); when neither works it stays and a warning says so. The one beside the hob is kept.
Each run is labelled AA, BB, CC, DD in order. Islands get their own sequence.
rules.note: Prefix word is not standardised: P1 used WALL-AA", P2 used ELEVATION-AA, P3 used bare AA.

rules.statement: Partly explained. The 'glass in the middle' seen in P2 and P4 is the chimney rule — those glass units flank the chimney. What still has no rule is P3, where the hob was on a third wall and the left wall came out all glass while the right came out all solid.
rules.open_question: Designer discretion, client choice, or a rule not visible in plan view?
evidence: P2 right: solid, glass, glass, solid  (solid at both ends)
P3: left wall all glass, right wall all solid
P4 bottom: dishrack, glass, glass, glass, solid  (solid at the corner end)
rules.hypothesis: Glass beside the chimney is settled. Glass elsewhere is still designer discretion or an unseen rule.

rules.statement: The user chooses 7ft (2140mm design height) or 8ft (2500mm design height); a 100mm top filler closes the tall stack.
evidence: P1 titleblock: 'Height Considered: 2500mm + Top Filler'
P4 titleblock: 'Height Considered: 2500mm'
855 counter + 560 backsplash + 1085 wall = 2500 = 2400 tall + 100 filler

rules.statement: An internal accessory takes the width of the cabinet holding it.
evidence: P3: 900 hob base -> 'Cutlery Tray Silverstone 900 mm'
P4: 600 hob base -> 'Cutlery Tray Silverstone 600 mm'
P4: 900 base     -> '2-Onion & Potato Basket 900 mm'

rules.statement: The sink base carries a pull-out waste bin, 14 litre x 2.
evidence: P1: 'space for waste bin 14 LTR x 2 & detergent holder'
P4: 'Plastic Pull Out Waste bin 14x2 ltr'

rules.statement: Base units are CJ or TTS, the client's choice. Wall, loft and mid units have no handle (NHX). Tall units are always TTS and can never be CJ.
rules.note: Handle is a project-level input, applied as a filter before layout runs; the solver never decides it. The legend's phrase 'tall cabinets STONE shutters' is not an exclusion — stone is the default material and glass is optional, so it simply describes the normal case.
rules.consequence: STD is the pre-rename value, not a separate handle. It resolves to the group's ordinary handle — TTS for base and tall, NHX for wall and loft — so the ~25 rows still carrying it are correct as they stand. No bulk edit needed.

rules.statement: Visible panels are exactly 20mm and must never be widened to absorb packing space. Use a visible panel on a tall cabinet only when its side is exposed to view, including the side above an adjoining base run. A tall side concealed against a wall uses a 40mm wall filler instead; the refrigerator's own sides are exempt (no-filler-beside-fridge). Ordinary gap fillers must be at least 30mm; corner fillers are at least 40mm. Panels and fillers are separate products.
rules.note: The 30mm minimum applies to ordinary gap fillers. Wall fillers at concealed tall sides are exactly 40mm. Automatic corner fillers remain 40-100mm; manually specified corner fillers may be up to 150mm. The designer may turn any filler into a visible panel (and back) from the edit sidebar: the panel is always exactly panel_width at the chosen end, and a wider filler keeps the remainder as a filler.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html editFillerToPanel() (sidebar 'Make visible panel' / 'Change to filler'); normalizeList() never merges a panel into a neighbouring filler. Param panel_width.

rules.statement: Only codes present in the updated cabinet sheet may be used. Modules exist for that list and nothing else.
rules.note: The engine's variable domain is the sheet. It may never invent a width. Odd widths in the sample drawings (1000, 920, 1070, 179) are outside it and are not a target to reproduce.

rules.statement: Any low-depth cabinet is 336mm deep. No exceptions.
rules.note: Applies to the BCL, BBL and TCL zones. Enforced on import — the TCL-SH-TTS-ST-HK rows carrying 560 are data errors.

rules.statement: Maximise usable cabinet storage across each complete run and minimise avoidable filler after satisfying all hard constraints. Compare combinations of catalogue widths, not a greedy largest-cabinet-first arrangement. Replacing a 900mm cabinet with 600mm plus 450mm is better when it uses 150mm of otherwise wasted filler and all clearances remain valid.
rules.note: Compare both sides of the refrigerator together, including the pantry and oven bank. Test the bank on either side, preserve included appliance functions, and use permitted anchor adjustments up to 100mm from the original positions. Required 20mm panels, 30mm countertop dropdowns and 40mm wall fillers are not wasted space. Prefer less movement when storage and filler are equal.

rules.statement: The hob base is 900 where it fits, otherwise 600. Take the largest possible.
evidence: P3 used 900
P4 used 600

rules.statement: The designer may choose the hob base's SHAPE and the SHAPE of the cabinet flanking it on either side. A shape is a catalogue internal configuration — "2LB+1HB", "1BL+1HF", "BPO" — never a width or a height. When a shape is chosen it is a hard constraint: the engine places that family and that configuration and solves only the width, taking the largest the run will take. If no width of the chosen shape fits, that is a hard failure reported against the choice — the engine never substitutes a different shape. A side left unchosen is solved as before.

overrides.hob-largest-that-fits: still picks the largest width, but only among units of the chosen shape
overrides.bottle-pullout-flanks-hob: Preserve the chosen flank and place the required bottle pullout immediately beyond an eligible flank when needed.
overrides.grain-trolley-required: A selected flank does not remove the grain trolley requirement; place the trolley elsewhere if needed.

evidence: Requested by the design team: pick the shape, let the engine size it.
rules.note: Chosen hob-side shapes are preserved. The required grain trolley is placed elsewhere when necessary, and the required bottle pullout may sit beyond a chosen flank.

rules.statement: Prefer equal-width cabinets flanking the hob — 900/900, 600/600 or 450/450, largest pair that fits. A preference, not a constraint: a grain drawer or bottle pullout on one side is equally acceptable.
evidence: P3: 600 | 150 BPO | 900 hob | 150 BPO | 600 — symmetric
P4: 600 | 600 hob | 300 BPO — asymmetric and valid, the pullout satisfies the rule

rules.statement: A sink always sits on a base sink unit. The pairing is mandatory.

Every kitchen includes a hob, chimney, sink, refrigerator, at least one bottle pullout and at least one grain trolley. The grain trolley may be elsewhere in the kitchen; the bottle pullout may be beside a hob-flanking cabinet. A tandem pantry and microwave/oven cabinet are preferred when they fit.
rules.note: Hob, main sink and refrigerator are required appliance anchors; the optional veggie sink is a separate anchor. The vegetable-basket requirement was cancelled by the user; every sink gets a dish rack above it (dish-rack-above-sink).

preferred.note: at least one, two at most — flour and rice
preferred beside the refrigerator; houses microwave and oven
Hard requirement — confirmed. Must be present in every kitchen.

rules.statement: Every used base corner carries one filler of at least 40mm on one adjacent run.
rules.note: The automatic solver chooses 40-100mm so the run can close. Manual fillers may be 40-150mm. What follows the filler is stated by blind-corner-snap.

rules.statement: At a blind or LeMans corner, keep the required filler of at least 40mm on the adjacent wall, followed by an ordinary cabinet. The blind cabinet opening shutter starts 40mm beyond that adjacent cabinet front face, measured along the wall carrying the blind cabinet from the inside corner. For a 600mm adjacent projection, the shutter starts at 640mm. This is the shutter position, not the start of the whole cabinet body. Allow 0-100mm of concealed space behind the blind cabinet instead of requiring it to touch the corner wall. Leave this hidden space empty; use fillers for visible leftover gaps.
evidence: P6: the run beside the blind corner began with a bottle pullout flush to the corner — no filler, nothing said.

overrides.no-dead-corners: Up to 100mm of concealed corner space is allowed behind the blind cabinet.
overrides.fill-small-remaining-spaces: Fill visible residual spaces; do not fill concealed corner space.

rules.note: Applies separately to base and upper corners using the actual adjacent cabinet front projection, including any depth offset. Base and upper blind cabinets remain on the same wall. Cabinet catalogue body dimensions stay unchanged. Track the opening shutter separately from the concealed blind section; all clearance, opening and collision checks remain in force.

rules.statement: Where a base or wall blind cabinet has a visible gap filler further along its run, use the concealed space behind the blind (up to 100mm) to take that filler up before leaving it visible. The filler need not touch the blind: the blind and every ordinary cabinet between it and the filler slide together toward the filler, which closes up against the next item. Only whole cabinets slide; a hob, sink, veggie sink, refrigerator, chimney, dishwasher, tall unit or other fixed item in that chain means nothing slides and the filler stays. If the filler is wider than the space available, absorb what fits so that the remaining filler is still at least 30mm.
evidence: Designer, 2026-10-04: blind 1150 | 500 | 300 bottle pullout | 77 filler | sink. The 77 is under the 100mm allowance, yet it was left as a visible filler beside the sink.
rules.note: Refines blind-corner-snap. Before this, only a filler touching the blind was absorbed, and the packer puts the leftover at the far end of the span, so it almost never was. The corner filler of at least 40mm required on the adjacent wall is a different piece and is never absorbed. Implemented in arrangeBlindFronts (core/engine.mjs).

rules.statement: A tall visible panel is handed by the side of the tall cabinet it sits on. Where a base run meets the tall cabinet on its left side, the panel is a LEFT visible panel; where the base run meets it on its right side, it is a RIGHT visible panel. A panel on an exposed end of a tall run follows the same rule by its side of the cabinet.
rules.note: Left is the lower wall offset (the 'from' end of the run), right the higher ('to' end), the same convention the renderer uses for LH/RH fillers. The catalogue stocks one VP-560-15 and one VP-336-15 with no left or right code, so the hand is recorded on the panel (side), carried into the plan and 3D view, and checked at every base/tall junction; it does not change the SKU or the price.

rules.statement: An exposed base run end requires a fixed 30mm countertop dropdown. At a base/tall junction, use one fixed 20mm tall visible side panel and no duplicate base dropdown. Touching base zones are continuous. Exposed wall run ends use fixed 20mm panels. At a free base or wall run end the panel sits directly on the last cabinet, never behind a filler; any leftover wall beyond the panel stays open and is either none or at least 200mm. Only when that would leave a thin sliver does a measured gap filler of at least 30mm close the run instead, between the last cabinet and the panel. A tall side concealed by a physical wall uses a 40mm wall filler; an exposed tall side uses a 20mm visible panel; a refrigerator at the end of a tall run needs neither (no-filler-beside-fridge). Reserve corner footprints before treating run ends.
rules.note: Never widen panels. Any residual space must be handled by a separate legal filler, a different cabinet packing, or reported anchor movement within the allowed 100mm.
rules.implementation: 3D (ui/renderer3d.js): every end panel stands sideways on the cabinet side it closes, as the visible panel model — the base 30mm dropdown and base panels as VP-560-15, wall run-end panels as VP-336-15, tall panels as before — handed by panelSide() (RH when a unit ends where the panel starts). Designer, 2026-10-21: base and wall ends were drawn as front filler strips (BFP/WFP), leaving the cabinet side bare.

rules.statement: The refrigerator is an appliance, not a cabinet, so it never gets a wall filler, visible panel or gap filler on its outer side. When the refrigerator is the last item at the end of a tall run, whether that end is a free end or faces a wall, nothing is placed beside it. The one exception is a refrigerator at the very end of its wall, against a room wall: it may stand up to 150mm (manual_filler_max) off that wall, and a gap filler (at least gap_filler_min) closes the space so the end looks seamless and clean (designer, 2026-10-17). Otherwise, if a leftover space between the refrigerator and that end is too small to hold any tall cabinet, it stays empty; it still counts as unused space when layouts are compared, so the refrigerator is not slid off the wall just to hide it. The tall cabinet on the refrigerator's other side is finished by its own rules as usual.
evidence: Designer, 2026-10-04: a filler was drawn between the refrigerator and the wall although the refrigerator sat between a tall cabinet and that wall.
rules.note: Exception to panel-vs-filler and run-end-treatment. A base/tall junction panel is unchanged. The engine marks the empty sliver with a non-rendered blocker (role 'empty space beside refrigerator', emptySpace) so fit scoring counts it as waste. Wall-end exception: core/engine.mjs fillTier('tall') places a 'gap filler' for a 30-150mm sliver at offset 0 / wall length where tallSideAgainstWall(); runEndProblems() skips trims when finding the refrigerator. Test: test/engine/engine.test.mjs.

rules.statement: The chimney sits directly above the hob.
rules.note: The chimney has no cabinet code — it is a client appliance that occupies wall-tier space with no SKU, so it displaces wall units rather than being one.

rules.statement: Prefer glass wall units on both sides of the chimney. If both cannot fit, keep the chimney valid and report the unmet preference.
evidence: P4 top run: Wall Glass Shutter | hob+chimney | Wall Glass Shutter
P2 cooking wall: solid, glass, glass, solid — the two glass units flank the chimney

rules.statement: When an eligible base corner exists and it fits, prefer at least one 1050mm LeMans corner. Otherwise use a 1150mm blind corner. Straight kitchens have no corner requirement.
rules.note: P2's corner label read as a plain blind rather than a LeMans, but that came off a compressed image and the rule is stated — treating it as my misreading, not an exception.

rules.statement: Hob and sink are at least 350mm apart, measured along the countertop path including around adjacent corners.
rules.note: A hard minimum edge-to-edge clearance. Non-adjacent walls are handled as separate runs.

rules.statement: A sink is never placed in a blind corner.

Strongly prefer symmetric wall cabinets beside the chimney. Map eligible base flank widths using 900 to 850, 600 to 550 and 450 to 450mm; when base flanks differ, use the larger mapped width for both wall cabinets. Choose the largest base-flank widths that also allow this upper pair to fit, preserving designer-selected shapes. Adjust the hob position by up to 100mm on its wall when this improves fit; report every movement. If no legal combination fits, retain the valid chimney layout and report that the preference could not be met.
rules.note: Width is solved across both tiers whenever the preferred pair fits their zones, openings, corners and tall footprints. The chimney itself remains mandatory; its matching wall-cabinet pair does not.
evidence: 900 | 600 hob | 900 = 2400 base, and 850 | 700 chimney | 850 = 2400 wall — the tiers close on the same total
P4 wall tier reads 550 either side, which is exactly 600 flank minus 50
The catalog stocks 850 and 550 wall units and no other odd widths — those two sizes exist BECAUSE of this rule

rules.statement: The chimney is always wider than the hob, by params.chimney_wider_than_hob_by (100mm). A 600 hob takes a 700 chimney; a 900 hob takes a 1000.
rules.note: The overhang is split evenly, so the chimney reaches 50mm past the hob on each side.

rules.statement: Every wall-run chimney gets a chimney panel aligned with the wall cabinets beside it: its top level with their tops and its face on the same plane as their shutters, covering the chimney above the hood. Width follows the hob: a 600 hob takes CP-700, a 900 hob takes CP-1000 (hob + params.chimney_wider_than_hob_by, the chimney width). Height follows the kitchen height, params.chimney_panel_height: 7ft takes 450, 8ft takes 600. Codes: CP-700-450-15, CP-700-600-15, CP-1000-450-15, CP-1000-600-15 (Panels sheet).
rules.note: The panel is the chimney's own cover, the one item exempt from chimney-front-clearance. Shown in 3D and the walkthrough; not yet in the BOQ or quote (pricing to be decided). An island chimney hung from a beam gets no panel.

rules.statement: Whenever a wall-tier unit or a beam is over the hob, the chimney model is placed above the hob. Nothing may be placed in front of it: no cabinet, panel, accessory or appliance may enter the chimney's own envelope or the params.chimney_front_clearance (600mm) directly in front of it, from the chimney's underside to the ceiling, across the chimney's full width.
rules.note: Enforced by the 3D renderer: the zone is reserved before anything else is placed and an intruding unit is left out of the scene and reported. Nothing is placed on or over the chimney either: its wall-tier slot gets no filler. The exceptions are the chimney's own panel (chimney-panel) and a backsplash the designer adds, which lies flat on the wall behind both the chimney and its panel. An island hob's chimney hangs from a beam and is kept clear on both faces.

rules.statement: A dishwasher is optional. When included, it sits immediately left or right of the sink.
evidence: P1 utility: dishwasher directly beside the sink run
P4: 'Space for Dishwasher' immediately right of the base sink cabinet
rules.note: Presence is a preference; adjacency is a hard conditional rule once included. Dishwasher is not an anchor.

rules.statement: The designer provides the starting positions of the hob, sink and refrigerator. Each may move along its own wall by up to 100mm from that starting position to improve cabinet fit and reduce wasted space, even when the original layout already fits. All movements must be reported.
rules.note: Keep appliance widths and walls, openings, separation rules and cabinet areas valid. Never accumulate adjustments beyond 100mm from the designer-provided starting position.

rules.statement: The optional 600mm veggie sink is separate from the main sink. Each has its own designer-selected cabinet position; no minimum or maximum distance applies between the two sinks. Both must fit their cabinet areas without overlapping fixtures or obstructing a door.

The designer can enter the refrigerator appliance width. Reserve an opening with 50mm clear space on each side: a 900mm refrigerator requires a 1000mm opening. Side clearances must remain empty and may not be filled with cabinets.
Hob, main sink, veggie sink and refrigerator are never placed in front of a door.
rules.note: Because the designer places these by hand, this is an INPUT VALIDATION rule — reject the placement with an error, do not silently move it.

rules.statement: Never place a cabinet or the refrigerator right beside a door: leave at least 50mm of bare wall on each side of every door, in the base, wall and tall rows. The 50mm stays bare: no filler or panel goes there.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs reserves a 'door side clearance' blocker on each side of a door in every tier (drawn as open wall); core/checkInput.mjs rejects an appliance within 50mm of a door, which the corrector slides clear. The zone tool keeps out the same 50mm (vendor/rules.js openings.doorClearEachSide reads it; it was a hard-coded 400mm, which stopped zones being drawn closer). Param door_side_clearance.

rules.statement: If the refrigerator is behind a door or within its swing, its nearest side is at least 800mm from the door's edge, measured along the wall (around the corner when the fridge is on the next wall). The swing side is the door's hinge side; sliding, doorless and outward-opening doors have no swing into the kitchen.
rules.implementation: core/checkInput.mjs (input validation); core/correct.mjs slides the fridge clear when it can, otherwise draws it with the rule listed as broken. Param fridge_door_swing_gap.

rules.statement: The main sink and veggie sink may sit in front of a window. A hob or refrigerator never may.
rules.note: Also input validation, same as the door rule.

rules.statement: Wall and tall cabinets are never placed in front of a window.

When a normal window (sliding or openable) ends less than 360mm from an inside corner, the adjoining wall takes no wall cabinet within 200mm of that corner; its wall cabinets start 200mm from the corner. Full-length and corner windows do not trigger this. That corner has no wall blind cabinet, so its base blind cabinet needs no matching upper.
seen_in: Designer, 2026-10-10: replaces the earlier 536mm (336mm depth + 200mm) trigger and reservation.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs windowCornerClearance(); params window_corner_trigger, window_corner_clearance

rules.statement: On the editing page, accessories are added to the cabinet that holds them, and a selected cabinet offers only the accessories that go in it: a drawer unit or hob base its low-back and high-back drawer accessories at its width (600 / 900; a 450 unit none), a bottle-pullout cabinet its Bottle Pull-Out (150 single, 300 double), a waste-bin pullout its Waste Bin Pull-Out, a LeMans corner its LeMans mechanism, a tall tandem pantry its Tandem Pantry mechanism, a 600 / 900 wall cabinet the Magic Pull Down (Double Tray). Mechanisms are offered as a tick, never added automatically. Each accessory is offered only where the Excel master's zone columns allow it (cooking, washing, cooling, island, other wall). One accessory per drawer, each at most once per cabinet. A pick belongs to its cabinet: replacing or deleting the cabinet removes it, and on regenerate it stays only on a cabinet of the same code in the same place. The hob's drawers and pictured side units share the HOB step's picks, and the sink cabinet shares the SINK step's. Accessories that do not go inside a cabinet (Kubos, Tark, Ceiling Hanging Unit, stone shelves, glass rolling shutter) are not offered on the editing page. Earlier kitchen-wide picks stay in the estimate until removed (designer, 2026-10-21).
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html cabAccSlots() / ACC_ZONES / drawerTypesOf() (what a cabinet holds), hobUnitForSel() (HOB step units), cabAccHtml() / toggleCabAcc() (editing panel; picks on seg.accs), cabAccItems() (estimate, priced at the cabinet width), carryCabAccs() (regenerate), zoneForSel() (now also the cooling zone near the fridge). Test: test/hob-accessories/hob-accessories.test.mjs.

rules.statement: In a hob cabinet look, the drawer units pictured beside the hob take accessories as well as the hob's own drawers: low-back items in low-back drawers, high-back items in high-back drawers, one accessory per drawer, and each accessory at most once in the hob zone (no repeats). A side unit offers the accessories for its own width (600 or 900; a 450 unit or a grain unit takes none). While choosing, a side unit is taken at the width its picture shows (900 for looks 1, 2 and 4, 600 for look 3), giving at most 7 / 5 / 5 / 5 accessories. The engine sizes the side units itself; when a generated side unit is a different width, the accessories it cannot take are removed, the designer is warned, and is asked to choose that cabinet's accessories again for the generated width (designer, 2026-10-21).
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html HOB_SIDE_PRESETS.sideWidth + presetSides() give each pictured drawer unit its drawers; hobUnits() / hobFlatAccList() / hobFreeDrawerFor() / toggleHobAcc() place accessories across hob and side drawers; hobBOQItems() prices each at its unit width; reconcileHobSideWidths() runs after Generate (toast + a 'hob-accessories' correction + a notice in the HOB step until Done) and after every editing-page change, and also checks the side unit's drawer shape. Test: test/hob-accessories/hob-accessories.test.mjs.

rules.statement: The refrigerator step offers four photo looks, and the kitchen generates exactly the towers the chosen picture shows: Glass Display Shelves = a glass tall unit on each side of the fridge (600mm each, 450mm each when 600 does not fit); Tandem Pantry + Oven Tower = tandem pantry on one side, microwave + oven tower on the other; Free-standing Fridge + Oven Tower = a free-standing fridge at the end of the wall with the oven tower beside it; Fridge with Tall Storage = one plain tall storage cabinet beside the fridge, no glass or appliances. With no look picked, the standard pantry + oven bank applies.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html FRIDGE_PICKS / syncFridgeStep() send options.fridgePick; server.mjs toEngineInput() puts it on the fridge anchor as `look`; core/engine.mjs expand() places the look's towers (tagged look:true, exempt from tandem-with-microwave pairing); core/correct.mjs deriveZones() sizes the auto tall band for the look. Test: test/fridge-look/fridge-look.test.mjs.

rules.statement: The chosen fridge look never limits where the fridge goes or which width can be entered: the designer picks a look and positions the fridge as they want. Only the ordinary placement rules apply (on the wall, clear of other fixtures, doors, windows and columns). When the look's towers do not fit beside the fridge, the engine reports it.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html fxDropValid() ignores S.fridge.pick; setFridgePick() no longer moves the fridge; core/engine.mjs warns 'fridge-look …: the towers in the chosen picture do not fit'. Test: test/ui-state/independent-fixtures.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A refrigerator panel closes the top of the fridge opening: the RFP code nearest the opening width (fridge + 50mm each side) — RFP-700, RFP-900 or RFP-1050, 300mm high — stretched (width and model) to run tall-to-tall: across the opening and any filler (up to 100mm) between it and the tall cabinets beside it. Its top is level with the real top of those tall cabinets' models and its face on their shutter plane; the fridge stands below it.
rules.implementation: ui/renderer3d.js tallBank fridge branch (RFP_W / RFP_H), model from Models/Additional Items/Refrigerator panels. 3D only, like the chimney panel. Test: test/models/models.test.mjs.

rules.statement: The refrigerator is never placed in front of a structural column. The designer cannot drop it there; if a setup has it there, the correction moves it, and if it cannot, the rule is listed as broken.
The designer draws the area where cabinets go, snapped to the wall edges, and draws it SEPARATELY for each tier — base, wall and tall. The engine fills within those zones and never outside them.
rules.note: Base and wall zones usually go together: drawing one on a wall adds the other over the same span when that wall has none of it yet. Either can then be adjusted or removed on its own.

rules.statement: Two kitchen heights are offered, 7ft and 8ft. The choice sets both the wall-unit and tall-unit height for the whole kitchen.
evidence: 8ft: 855 counter + 560 backsplash + 1085 wall = 2500 = 2400 tall + 100 filler
7ft: 855 counter + 560 backsplash + 725  wall = 2140 = 2040 tall + 100 filler
rules.note: This is what decides wall 725 vs 1085 — it was never a per-run choice. Both catalog wall heights and both tall heights pair up exactly, one pair per option.

rules.statement: LHS/RHS applies to single-shutter units. Either may be used — handing is unconstrained for now.
rules.note: Unblocks code emission: the engine picks a hand arbitrarily. Revisit if door-swing or adjacency turns out to matter.

rules.statement: At least one grain trolley is required in every kitchen, and at most two. Its position is flexible: it may be after two or three cabinets from the hob, or elsewhere in the kitchen. It does not have to touch the hob. Prefer a second when space permits.
rules.note: Presence is mandatory; immediate adjacency to the hob is not. Designer-selected hob flanks do not remove this requirement.

rules.statement: The tandem pantry is preferred and, when included, is placed beside the refrigerator.
The tandem pantry and the microwave + oven tall unit are preferred, and only ever as a pair: if one cannot be placed, neither is.
Preferred tall models form one contiguous block beside the fixed refrigerator when space permits.
rules.note: The refrigerator is the only tall anchor. Tandem pantry and oven unit remain preferred; no countertop-adjacency requirement applies to the microwave/oven cabinet.

rules.statement: Where a structural column intrudes into a run, low-depth cabinets (336) must be used. This is why the low-depth zones exist — BCL, BBL and TCL. For a column partway along a wall, the low-depth cabinet stands forward so its front lines up with the full-depth (560mm) cabinets beside it, leaving a gap behind it; it only stands further out if the column is deeper than that gap. Only a corner column is measured from its own face (column-in-corner).
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs geometryProblems(): offset = max(column depth, 560 - cabinet depth) for a mid-wall column, column depth for a corner column. Tested in test/geometry/geometry.test.mjs.
rules.note: Two consequences. (1) Depth is NOT constant along a run: 560 normally, 336 at a column, so the engine carries depth per segment, not per run. (2) The countertop follows that stepped profile, so its area is the sum of per-segment length x depth — never overall length x 560. Column positions come in with the room like doors and windows; P1's architect drawing marks them as C2.

rules.statement: When a column stands flush in an inside corner and is shallower than the cabinet depth on both walls (560mm base, 336mm wall), the corner is measured from the column face: the blind or LeMans cabinet and its wall blind stand against the column, the adjoining run keeps its usual return, and the strip beside the column is concealed corner space. The designer may also slide a corner cabinet along its wall into empty space, up to a column. A bigger column blocks the corner as before.
The refrigerator should be clear of both the hob and the sink, and the work triangle between the three should stay manageable.
rules.note: Soft, and deliberately without a number — no threshold was given, unlike hob-sink which is 350. Since the designer places all three anchors by hand, this reads as guidance for them rather than a solver constraint. Give it a millimetre value only if it ever needs enforcing.

rules.statement: Fit catalogue cabinets first and close remaining visible spaces with separate gap fillers of at least 30mm, placed only where no-filler-between-cabinets allows. If a remainder is smaller than 30mm, change packing or adjust anchors within their authorized tolerance; do not create a thinner filler or widen a panel. Required wall fillers are 40mm and corner fillers at least 40mm. Reserved cabinet footprints, openings and concealed blind-corner space remain empty.
rules.note: Ordinary gap fillers remain smaller than the narrowest eligible cabinet. Concealed space up to 100mm behind blind corners is exempt; moving a blind cabinet must not leave a visible filler below 30mm.

rules.statement: A gap filler is never placed between two cabinets, in the base or the wall row, and never beside the sink. A filler may only sit at a run end: against a wall, a corner filler, a tall unit, a door or window, or reserved space. Leftover space is moved there by sliding the ordinary cabinets; beside a blind or LeMans corner it is hidden in the concealed corner space (up to 100mm); otherwise the hob, sink or refrigerator moves within its 100mm tolerance so the run closes exactly. If none of that closes it, no filler is placed: the gap is reported for the designer.
rules.note: Replaces the earlier practice of fillers on both sides of the sink. Tall runs keep their own rules (wall filler, visible panel, no-filler-beside-fridge).

rules.statement: Where two tiers meet on the same wall, the boundary the designer drew may slide by up to params.zone_boundary_tolerance (100mm) if that lets both tiers close. A little more tall and a little less base makes no practical difference.
rules.note: Applied only as a repair when a layout otherwise fails, one boundary at a time, and never far enough to push an anchor out of its host zone. The move is reported as a note so the designer sees what was adjusted.

rules.statement: The hob, sink and refrigerator may each be repositioned by up to params.anchor_tolerance (100mm) along their own wall to improve the cabinet fit and reduce wasted space. This is allowed even if the original layout already fits. Compare valid arrangements by unused closure space and cabinet storage, using smaller movement to break ties. Report each original and new position.
evidence: Sweep: 25 rooms that failed as drawn closed with a 25–75mm slide of the fridge; none needed more than 75mm.
rules.note: Several anchors may move in one layout, but each stays within 100mm of its original designer position. All input and placement checks still apply. Ordinary anchor-only adjustments within this allowance are authorized; changes to cabinet areas use the separate zone-review flow.

overrides.anchors-are-designer-input: The designer's position is the starting point. Movements within 100mm may improve either a failing layout or an already fitting layout.

rules.statement: Never report that a kitchen cannot be made. When the designer's setup cannot be fitted as given, make slight corrections until it fits, choosing the smallest: an appliance (hob, sink, veggie sink, refrigerator) may slide along its own wall by at most 300mm — it never moves to another wall — and a cabinet zone edge (base, wall or tall band) may move by at most 300mm; zones are never added or removed. The room itself is fixed and is never changed: room dimensions, doors, windows and structures (beams, columns). Show every correction under the header "Corrections made to draw this kitchen".
evidence: Stated by the business, 2026-09-29.
rules.note: Implemented in core/correct.mjs (correctKitchen / describeCorrections), called from /api/build after the bounded fitting search. Missing designer inputs (invalid walls, no handle type, island not placed) are not layout failures and are still asked for.

overrides.anchor-tolerance: The 100mm allowance still governs silent fit improvements; up to 300mm, a correction is made and listed instead of the build failing.

rules.statement: Where a base and wall zone share a run end, their finished runs must reach that same boundary. A packing failure must not silently leave one tier shorter.
rules.note: Align the overall run ends. Individual door seams and the independent corner footprints are not required to match. Deliberately separate wall zones beside windows remain separate.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs wallBaseEndProblems(), run on every layout; a mismatch is reported as a problem naming the unfinished tier. Tested in test/alignment/alignment.test.mjs.

rules.statement: In editing, the designer may place any cabinet type in any space, whatever zone was drawn there: a tall cabinet in a base zone, a base cabinet in a tall zone, a wall cabinet where no wall zone was drawn. Structures still win: no cabinet may run into a column or reach up into a beam's drop.
rules.note: The picked cabinet decides what it becomes, not the zone. A tall cabinet stands on the floor, so it is placed from the base row, and the wall cabinets and lofts over its span are removed. Doors and windows keep their wall.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html editReplacePick() with structureClash() and clearUpperOver(); drawPlanElev() offers open upper slots while editing; relocateSelected() lets tall units be dragged and applies the same structure check. Tested in test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A door or window of any type can be as narrow as 500mm.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html OPENING_MIN (placing, resizing and corner-window legs); replaces the old per-type door minimums (900-1200mm) and the 400mm window minimum.

rules.statement: A column's width and depth, and a beam's width, can be anything up to the room's own size. A column or beam standing against a wall shows the space left on each side of it, and that space can be set like a door's or window's.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html structMax() (room extent along x/y), computeGapsForWall() + moveStructByDelta(). Tested in test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: On the layout page the designer can draw extra walls inside the room. A drawn wall stays inside the room, runs straight, stops at the first wall it meets, and its ends snap onto room walls or other drawn walls, so two drawn walls can close off an area. A drawn wall is solid floor to ceiling: no cabinet may stand in it.
rules.note: Horizontal or vertical, whichever way the drag leans; 115mm thick; at least 200mm long.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html toggleWallDraw()/wallDrawStart()/wallDrawEnd()/commitWallDraw(), stored as a structure of type 'partition'; server.mjs projects it onto any room wall it touches like a column; drawn solid in the 2D plan and as plain wall in 3D. Tested in test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Empty space on a wall is not offered as an extend area where a cabinet on another wall already stands, or where a cabinet there would block that cabinet's doors or drawers. A leftover too narrow for a corner filler plus the narrowest cabinet is not offered either.
rules.note: Front access is taken as deep as the adjoining cabinet itself. A blind corner's concealed section has no doors, so only its footprint counts. Recomputed after every edit, so the space frees up again when the other cabinet moves or is deleted.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html markOccupiedSpace(), run from recalcPositions() and normalizeReservedSpaces(); params corner_filler_min and the 150mm narrowest base cabinet. Tested in test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: An island is optional and is added only at the designer's request when adequate space exists.
Draw cabinet zones and place surrounding core fixtures before confirming island size or position. Revalidate against generated cabinets.

Use millimetres. The minimum island cabinet length is 1200mm and the minimum depth 600mm, in either orientation. The countertop overhangs 30mm past the cabinets at each end, so a 1200mm island has a 1260mm top; a longer end projection must be entered explicitly.

Use eligible catalogue cabinets for storage. Island length is a designer-entered whole-millimetre dimension, with no fixed preset maximum; the room and clearances determine its limit. Close residual storage-row gaps with cut-to-size panels. Seating-only islands do not require cabinet modules.
Provide at least 1050mm clear working aisle between finished island edges and surrounding cabinets or appliances.
With 600mm-deep wall cabinets, the island edge starts at least 1650mm from that wall. Deeper projections increase the offset.
Reserve cabinet depth only where a base or tall cabinet zone or actual cabinet exists. Do not reserve it along empty wall sections.
Provide 950mm for walking-only passages. Use the greatest applicable working, walking or seating clearance.
Measure clearances between finished surfaces, including countertop overhangs and appliance projections.
Calculate island length and depth independently and check the complete footprint against the actual room outline, zones, obstacles and openings.

Allow movement and rotation only where the full island footprint and required clearances fit. During dragging, shade the permitted placement area, show blocked positions as a preview, and stop the island at the last valid boundary. Reject invalid coordinate and rotation edits.

Show up to four illustrated standard-width choices: 600, 900, 976 and 1200mm, with their purpose and a starting length that fits. Group rotations instead of listing duplicates. Provide a prominent custom length field; suggested lengths are not restrictions.

Clicking an island or size option opens its right sidebar with exact dimensions, position, rotation, seating capacity and per-side clearances. Before Generate Design the designer chooses only the island type and size: no cabinet modules, module widths or cabinet arrangement are shown on the plan, the type cards or the sidebar. The cabinet specification appears only after Generate Design, on the Review screen.
Keep entrances, door swings and access routes clear. Check cabinet and appliance opening space without collisions.

Use four standard finished widths: 600mm storage only, 900mm seating only, 976mm seating plus storage, and 1200mm double-row storage. Seating-only uses a supported tabletop with no storage cabinets. Finish exposed cabinet ends and backs within the fixed width.

Seating plus storage is 976mm wide: 600mm storage plus 376mm clear seating overhang. Seating-only is 900mm wide. Keep finishes within these standard widths; show additional end finishes in the length.
Measure 376mm clear seating overhang from the finished cabinet back to the countertop edge. Supports and panels must preserve knee space.
Allocate 650mm of usable seating edge per person. Exclude supports, legs, unusable corners and selected blocked seating spans.
Reserve 1150mm from the finished seating edge to any opposing obstruction where people pass behind seated users.
Seating is optional and side-specific. Recalculate the footprint and clearances when it changes. Adjacent sides must not share a seat corner.
Main and veggie sinks may be independently assigned to the island. No distance requirement applies between the two sinks. Confirm plumbing and preparation space.
An island hob is explicit. Preserve existing hob-to-sink separation and selected cabinet shapes; verify extraction and the appliance's countertop and installation clearances.
Confirm a feasible water and drainage route for island sinks after the cabinet arrangement is established.
Check overhang support against the selected countertop material and construction. Unverified support or appliance requirements must remain unresolved, never assumed passed.
Recalculate options whenever zones, cabinet placement, fixtures, openings or island features change.

If room or cabinet changes invalidate an existing island, keep it visible and explain the failed clearances. Prevent new invalid placements. Never silently resize, rotate or relocate a saved island; a cancelled drag restores its original position.

Countertop and backsplash stone are both ₹551/sqft (material, Section A). Installation is billed separately in Section B: countertop ₹780/sqft, backsplash ₹300/sqft, cabinets ₹280/sqft. Cabinet installation is measured on the same carcass net sqft the cabinets are priced on, never on shutter area. Material and installation are never combined in one line, so nothing is charged twice. Backsplash area is the dado only: along each wall, wherever a countertop runs under a wall cabinet (or the hob's chimney slot), the wall from the countertop top to that cabinet's underside. No backsplash behind tall units, doors, windows or open wall.
rules.note: The live values are read from data/rates.json (rows by item); test/pricing checks that file against params.quote_rates.

rules.statement: A base or wall run that reaches the end of its wall where a solid perpendicular wall stands is closed by that wall, not exposed, even when the perpendicular wall carries no cabinets there. It gets no countertop dropdown or end panel and leaves no open wall: cabinets run up to the wall and any leftover is a gap filler against the wall.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs solve(): after corners are resolved, each base/wall zone end at offset 0 or the wall length whose side meets a non-open room wall (tallSideAgainstWall) is added to cornerEnds, so packing closes it with a gap filler and runEndProblems does not ask for a dropdown. Test: test/run-end/wall-closed-ends.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A cabinet band the designer drew into a corner or up to a wall end stays there. Corrections (kitchen-always-drawn-with-corrections) may move an appliance or a band's inner edge, but never pull a band edge away from a wall end; what cannot be fixed that way is reported instead of leaving dead space in the corner.
rules.implementation: core/correct.mjs candidates(): a band edge at 0 or the wall length is never shifted. Test: test/run-end/wall-closed-ends.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A manual edit never pushes a cabinet run past the end of its wall. Replacing a cabinet with a wider one may use the open space in that run; if it still does not fit, the replacement is refused and the designer is told how many mm are missing.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html editReplacePick(): the run is snapshotted, and the edit is rolled back with a message if the run would end beyond the wall length (an overrun saved by an older edit is not made worse). Move and corner slide already stay inside their run.

rules.statement: A mid-height wall cabinet stands on the countertop and rises to the top of the wall cabinets. It is usually near the fridge, but there is no placement condition. When the designer puts one in a wall-cabinet slot, it is placed on the countertop and the height variant (1290 / 1650) whose top meets the existing wall-cabinet top is used. Only mid-height wall cabinets stand on the countertop: any other wall cabinet put in the wall row (including where a mid cabinet was deleted) hangs level with the row's other wall cabinets, or 565 mm (the dado) above the countertop when there are none.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html editReplacePick(): an MD-/MDW- code picked in the wall row gets z = countertop (heights.baseTop) and is swapped for the same code at the height that reaches the slot's (or the row's non-mid) wall-cabinet top; with no such variant it is placed and a warning names the mismatch. Any other wall-row pick gets z = the first other non-mid wall cabinet's z, else baseTop + dado. Test: test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A base blind cabinet picked from the library during editing is treated like a generated blind corner: its concealed end is the end nearer the wall corner and its door starts past the adjoining run's front plus the blind shutter clearance. On the adjoining wall it occupies only the space its body stands in, not a door-front zone across its concealed part.
rules.implementation: ui/builder.html editReplacePick(): a BB-/BBL- code in the base row becomes kind 'corner' with corner.end and shutter {x0,x1} (base depth + params.blind_shutter_clearance from the nearer wall end); markOccupied() then uses the shutter span for the front zone. Test: test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: While editing, the edge between two neighbouring empty pieces of a base run (open space, extend area, dead space, a corner reservation or a filler) can be dragged to resize them, or dragged to the end to merge them into one space the designer can use however they want — e.g. to take a corner back for a blind corner on that wall. A cabinet standing on the adjoining wall still marks the space it occupies (and its open space) as occupied. The edge between a cabinet and the empty space beside it can be dragged too: the cabinet slides with it (keeping its width) into that space. A cabinet is dragged with a single press — pressing it selects it and drags it in one go.
rules.implementation: ui/detailed-plan.js emptyJoint() + .emptyjoint handles (data-cab on a cabinet/empty edge); ui/builder.html startEmptyJointDrag()/moveEmptyBoundary()/moveCabinetEdge() → relocateSelected(); startModDrag() selects on press; markOccupied() also cuts open space. Test: test/ui-state/ui-state.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Worktop is drawn over base-row open space (a deleted cabinet or filler) only when a base cabinet stands right beside it on that run; otherwise the open space has no worktop, so a slab never floats with nothing under it.
rules.implementation: ui/renderer3d.js run loop, seg.open branch: worktop() only if the previous or next non-zero-width segment is a non-tall cabinet/anchor/corner.

rules.statement: Where base runs meet at an inside corner, the first 600mm of each wall (the 560mm return plus the corner filler) belongs to the corner, whichever wall the blind takes. Cabinets placed beside the hob (grain trolley, bottle pullout, or a flank the designer named) never go there. If a flank cannot fit outside it, the hob moves (within the correction limits) or the flank is reported; the corner is never given up for it.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs expand(): cornerKeep lists those spans and flankFits() rejects any hob flank overlapping one. core/correct.mjs tries appliance and band moves in 50mm steps (up to 300mm) so a hob can land in the narrow window that fits a flank beside the corner. Tests: test/engine/engine.test.mjs (cornered flank), test/run-end/wall-closed-ends.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Plan import is phase 1 of 2: structure first, cabinetry later. Gemini 3.8 Flash finds the kitchen on the uploaded PDF or image. The designer then drags along one wall of it (A to B) and types its real length; how that wall is drawn on THIS plan (solid, or two face lines with their weight, spacing and fill, hollow or hatched, and the ink colour) is learned from the stroke, and the boundary is traced by following only ink drawn the same way, so counter edges, zone lines, dimensions, furniture and text are not walls. Where the outline leaves that style it is a door (nothing drawn across), a window (something else drawn across, e.g. glass lines in place of the hatch) or an open side; solid blocks in or against the wall are columns. The guess is shown on the plan for the designer to confirm before the Layout page: they can click a door or window to change it (door, window, opening without a door, not an opening), mark a second wall when the plan draws walls in two styles, take the other side of the marked wall, redo, or read the plan with AI instead. On confirm the Layout page opens pre-filled with walls, doors, windows, open sides and columns. Hob, sink and cabinet zones are phase 2 and are not filled from the trace; the AI read (the fallback, and the multi-kitchen 'open all as rooms' path) still pre-fills them, placing anything that cannot stand where the plan shows it in a note, never forcing it in.
rules.implementation: ui/wall-trace.js WallTrace.learn() (wall style + ink-colour mask from the stroke) -> trace() (cross-section bands, collinear gap bridging, flood fill, orthogonalize, takeColumns, readSides) -> scaleFrom() -> toDraft(); ui/builder.html lockKitchenRegion() -> openWallMark() -> renderWallMark()/wallTraceRun() -> renderWallPreview() (wtCycleOpening) -> wallTraceConfirm() -> applyVisionExtract(). Kitchen found by plan-read.mjs findKitchens() (/api/kitchen-detect); AI fallback readKitchenWithAi() -> readKitchen()/toDraft() (/api/vision-extract) -> applyDrawnCabinetry(). Tests: test/wall-trace/wall-trace.test.mjs, test/plan-read/plan-read.test.mjs.

rules.statement: A hob, sink or veggie sink may sit flush with the end of its cabinet zone. No cabinet is required beside it on that side (a hob is flanked only on its other side), its countertop dropdown sits just outside the zone where the wall is clear, and a hob's chimney may hang past the wall zone by its own overhang over bare wall, never over an opening or a tall zone. No rule may keep an appliance away from a zone end.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs expand(): atZoneEnd() drops the flank on a side flush with the base zone end; chimneyFits() allows the chimney overhang (zoneOverhang flag skips the in-zone check). solve(): a flush hob/sink end gets its 'countertop return' outside the zone; runEndProblems() and wallBaseEndProblems() accept it and the overhanging chimney. Test: test/engine/engine.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Wall cabinets hang from counter_height + backsplash up to the kitchen's design height. A window whose sill height plus window height leaves it wholly below or wholly above that band does not block wall cabinets: a wall zone may be drawn across it and wall cabinets may be placed in front of it. A window that overlaps the band still keeps wall cabinets out, and tall cabinets never stand in front of a window.
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs windowClearOfWall()/windowHitsTier() used by openingFree(), the opening blockers, geometryProblems(), corners() and windowCornerClearance(); ui/builder.html windowClearOfWall() in zoneBlocksOn(). Test: test/engine/engine.test.mjs.

rules.statement: Whenever a sink cabinet is placed, a wall dish rack cabinet always goes above the sink. Its width follows the sink: a 600mm sink gets a 600mm dish rack; a sink of 900mm or more gets the 900mm dish rack. If a window is above the sink, the dish rack goes in the wall cabinet immediately left or right of the window, whichever side is nearer the sink. If there is no room for it there (e.g. wall blind corners take the wall cabinet run either side of the window), no dish rack is placed.
rules.note: Re-established by the user on 2026-10-19; it was previously recorded as refuted. 'No room' is a warning, not a release block (user, 2026-10-19: 'dont put dish rack there'). Sinks under 900mm other than 600mm (e.g. 750) also get the 600mm rack. A single-door 600mm rack is handed away from the sink centre (LHS when over or left of it). Island sinks are exempt (no wall above).
rules.implementation: core/engine.mjs solve(): before packing the wall tier, tries the rack (WC-AC-...-DSH code at the design-height wall size, dishRackFor()) flush over the sink or flush against the window, keeping it only if the wall run still packs cleanly; otherwise packs the run and placeDishRacks() swaps 1-3 plain wall cabinets for the rack plus an exact re-pack. Neither fits: a warning and no rack. Test: test/dish-rack/dish-rack.test.mjs.

open_questions: Resolved: corrected cabinet codes are authoritative when their embedded dimensions disagree with spreadsheet dimension columns.

params._note: Every number in these rules is a tunable default, not a constant. Change it here.
params._counter_height: 720 carcass + 100 legs + 30 top (spec DV-049). Was 855 by subtraction.
params._backsplash: wall-unit gap above counter; 450-600 allowed, 565 default (spec DV-154). Was 560.
params._anchor_tolerance: Each appliance may move at most 100mm from its original designer position, including to improve an already fitting design. Report every movement; keep all safety and geometry checks.

quote_rates._note: ₹ per sqft, confirmed by the designer 2026-09-30. Source of truth for billing is data/rates.json; these must match it.
quote_rates.backsplash_area_basis: opt-in: only the regions the designer adds in the Elevation, on bare wall (never behind a cabinet; the chimney slot is bare for its full height, so the stone does run behind the chimney and its panel); cut area includes 10mm behind each cabinet/countertop edge it touches, billed x 1.25; slab 2440x1220 (ui/backsplash.js)

out_of_scope: Dado (1780 / 2600) — explicitly not needed for now.
L-corner units (BLC / WLC / TLC) — planned later; their 10-field codes parse but are not placed yet.
Costing and pricing — the sheet carries sqft, panel and shutter counts, but no pricing rules have been given.
Minimum viable run length — not needed, because the designer places all three anchors.

cancelled.reason: User cancelled point 24: countertop beside microwave/oven cabinet.
User cancelled point 35: no automatic preference, placement requirement or release block for the vegetable basket. The dish rack half was re-established on 2026-10-19 as dish-rack-above-sink.
User now requires fillers wherever a small space cannot accept a cabinet, including both sides of the sink.
